properties.nom: From Chambly to Michilimackinac: an engagé's journey (1805)
properties.description: Hired on 25 January 1805 for Michilimackinac, Provost left in the spring with the canoes of Parker, Gerrard, Ogilvy & Co.: from Lachine the brigade went up the Ottawa to Mattawa, crossed Lake Nipissing, ran down the French River to Georgian Bay and followed the north shore of Lake Huron to Mackinac Island — about 1,500 km and some thirty portages in five to six weeks.
properties.sources: Société historique de Saint-Boniface, base de données des contrats des voyageurs (archivesshsb.mb.ca), fiche « Provost, Etienne », contrat du 25 janvier 1805 devant le notaire Jonathan A. Gray (BAnQ, microfilm M620/1535), consultée le 20 novembre 2026 ; Vaugeois, Denis, « Provost, Québec - Provo, Salt Lake, Utah ? Des liens historiques et généalogiques », Le Devoir, 16-17 février 2002 (coupure du Drive de l'auteur, dossier ETIENNE_PROVOST_AUDUBON)
properties.note: Classic route of the Montreal canoes; the contract gives the destination, the route is reconstructed.

properties.nom: With Philibert to the upper Arkansas
properties.description: Joseph Philibert's party reaches the upper Arkansas by way of the Missouri and then the Kansas plains.
properties.sources: Tykal, Jack B., “Provost, Etienne”, Utah History Encyclopedia, Salt Lake City, University of Utah Press, 1994 (copy in the author's Drive, t_000690.pdf; uen.org)

properties.nom: The Chouteau-De Mun expedition
properties.description: Leaving St. Louis in September 1815, Chouteau and De Mun follow the Arkansas to the mountains, then head down to Taos.
properties.sources: Roy, Alain, “Sur la piste de Santa Fe, 1721-1880”, in Frenette, Yves, Étienne Rivard and Marc St-Hilaire (ed.) (2012), La francophonie nord-américaine, Québec, PUL, series “Atlas historique du Québec”, p. 103; Tykal, Jack B., “Provost, Etienne”, Utah History Encyclopedia, Salt Lake City, University of Utah Press, 1994 (copy in the author's Drive, t_000690.pdf; uen.org)

properties.nom: Prisoners on the way to Santa Fe
properties.description: Arrested in May 1817, Chouteau and De Mun's men are taken under escort to Santa Fe.
properties.sources: Roy, Alain, “Sur la piste de Santa Fe, 1721-1880”, in Frenette, Yves, Étienne Rivard and Marc St-Hilaire (ed.) (2012), La francophonie nord-américaine, Québec, PUL, series “Atlas historique du Québec”, p. 103; Old Santa Fe: A Magazine of History, Archaeology, Genealogy and Biography, vol. 1, Santa Fe, 1913-1914, p. 375 (archive.org)
properties.note: The exact place of arrest, on the upper Arkansas, is approximate.

properties.nom: Released: the return to St. Louis
properties.description: Stripped of their furs, the freed prisoners make their way back to St. Louis across the plains.
properties.sources: Roy, Alain, “Sur la piste de Santa Fe, 1721-1880”, in Frenette, Yves, Étienne Rivard and Marc St-Hilaire (ed.) (2012), La francophonie nord-américaine, Québec, PUL, series “Atlas historique du Québec”, p. 103

properties.nom: From St. Louis to Taos by the Santa Fe Trail
properties.description: Around 1822, Provost returns to New Mexico by the Santa Fe Trail, which Becknell has just opened.
properties.sources: Tykal, Jack B., “Provost, Etienne”, Utah History Encyclopedia, Salt Lake City, University of Utah Press, 1994 (copy in the author's Drive, t_000690.pdf; uen.org)

properties.nom: From Taos to the Uinta Basin by the north branch of the Old Spanish Trail
properties.description: Provost and Leclerc reach the Uinta country by the San Luis Valley, the Gunnison and the Colorado valley, the route of the Taos trappers.
properties.sources: Nelson, Jack William (1996), “The North Branch of the “Old Spanish Trail””, Journal of the Western Slope, vol. 11, no. 4, PDF p. 37 (author's Drive); Nelson, Jack William (2003), Forgotten Pathfinders Along the North Branch of the Old Spanish Trail, 1650-1850, PDF p. 40-41 (author's Drive)
properties.note: Schematic line of the north branch.

properties.nom: From the Uinta to Utah Lake
properties.description: The party heads west by the Duchesne and the Strawberry, then down to Utah Lake and the Jordan.
properties.sources: Tykal, Jack B., “Provost, Etienne”, Utah History Encyclopedia, Salt Lake City, University of Utah Press, 1994 (copy in the author's Drive, t_000690.pdf; uen.org); “Etienne Provost”, historytogo.utah.gov (Utah State Historical Society), accessed November 2026

properties.nom: The escape through the Wasatch
properties.description: The survivors of the massacre escape northeast through the Wasatch, then return to the Green and White river country for the winter.
properties.sources: “Etienne Provost”, historytogo.utah.gov (Utah State Historical Society), accessed November 2026; Nelson, Jack William (1996), “The North Branch of the “Old Spanish Trail””, Journal of the Western Slope, vol. 11, no. 4, PDF p. 37 (author's Drive)

properties.nom: Spring 1825: toward the Weber
properties.description: In the spring, Provost resumes hunting toward the Weber, where he meets Ogden.
properties.sources: Tykal, Jack B., “Provost, Etienne”, Utah History Encyclopedia, Salt Lake City, University of Utah Press, 1994 (copy in the author's Drive, t_000690.pdf; uen.org)

properties.nom: From the Weber to Fruitland
properties.description: Provost heads back southeast into the Duchesne basin, where he meets Ashley.
properties.sources: Tykal, Jack B., “Provost, Etienne”, Utah History Encyclopedia, Salt Lake City, University of Utah Press, 1994 (copy in the author's Drive, t_000690.pdf; uen.org)

properties.nom: With Ashley to the first rendezvous
properties.description: Provost guides Ashley by the Duchesne and the Strawberry, then north across the Uintas to Henry's Fork.
properties.sources: Tykal, Jack B., “Provost, Etienne”, Utah History Encyclopedia, Salt Lake City, University of Utah Press, 1994 (copy in the author's Drive, t_000690.pdf; uen.org); Nelson, Jack William (2003), Forgotten Pathfinders Along the North Branch of the Old Spanish Trail, 1650-1850, PDF p. 40 (author's Drive)

properties.nom: The return by the Missouri
properties.description: From the Green River, Provost reaches the Missouri and goes down it to St. Louis, where he is back in September 1826.
properties.sources: Hafen, LeRoy R., “Etienne Provost”, in Hafen (ed.), The Mountain Men and the Fur Trade of the Far West, Glendale, Arthur H. Clark, vol. 6 (1968), p. 371-386; mentioned p. 376; Hafen, LeRoy R. (1968), “Etienne Provost, Mountain Man and Utah Pioneer”, Utah Historical Quarterly, vol. 36, no. 2
properties.note: Hypothetical route; the stop at Fort Lookout comes from Hafen's sketch.

properties.nom: St. Louis to Fort Floyd: in McKenzie's service
properties.description: Provost goes up the Missouri to McKenzie's post at the mouth of the Yellowstone.
properties.sources: Dolin, Eric Jay (2010), Fur, Fortune, and Empire: The Epic History of the Fur Trade in America, New York, W. W. Norton, PDF p. 325 (author's Drive); Hafen, LeRoy R., “Etienne Provost”, in Hafen (ed.), The Mountain Men and the Fur Trade of the Far West, Glendale, Arthur H. Clark, vol. 6 (1968), p. 371-386; mentioned p. 377

properties.nom: In search of the free trappers
properties.description: From the mouth of the Yellowstone, Provost heads up into Crow country and the mountains to win the free trappers over to the American Fur Company.
properties.sources: Dolin, Eric Jay (2010), Fur, Fortune, and Empire: The Epic History of the Fur Trade in America, New York, W. W. Norton, PDF p. 325 (author's Drive); Chittenden, Hiram Martin (1902), The American Fur Trade of the Far West, New York, Francis P. Harper, vol. 1, p. 305-306 (archive.org)

properties.nom: With Fontenelle and Drips: Bayou Salade and Ham's Fork
properties.description: Setting out from the Missouri, the American Fur Company caravan reaches the Bayou Salade, then the Ham's Fork rendezvous.
properties.sources: Hafen, LeRoy R., “Etienne Provost”, in Hafen (ed.), The Mountain Men and the Fur Trade of the Far West, Glendale, Arthur H. Clark, vol. 6 (1968), p. 371-386; mentioned p. 379-380

properties.nom: The fur barge goes down to Bellevue
properties.description: The season's furs go down to Bellevue, by the Platte and then the Missouri.
properties.sources: Chittenden, Hiram Martin (1902), The American Fur Trade of the Far West, New York, Francis P. Harper, vol. 1, p. 475 (archive.org)
properties.note: Hypothetical route; the Platte is barely navigable and furs often traveled by mule to the Missouri.

properties.nom: The 1837 caravan to the Horse Creek rendezvous
properties.description: Second in command of the American Fur Company caravan, Provost follows the Platte and South Pass route to the Green River rendezvous, with the painter Miller.
properties.sources: Vaugeois, Denis, “Provost, Québec - Provo, Salt Lake, Utah ? Des liens historiques et généalogiques”, Le Devoir, 16-17 February 2002 (clipping in the author's Drive, folder ETIENNE_PROVOST_AUDUBON); Tykal, Jack B., “Provost, Etienne”, Utah History Encyclopedia, Salt Lake City, University of Utah Press, 1994 (copy in the author's Drive, t_000690.pdf; uen.org)

properties.nom: With Nicollet, from Fort Pierre to Devils Lake
properties.description: The Nicollet and Frémont expedition crosses the Coteau du Missouri and goes up the James River to Devils Lake.
properties.sources: Nicollet, Joseph-Nicolas (1841), Report Intended to Illustrate a Map of the Hydrographical Basin of the Upper Mississippi River, Senate, 26th Congress, 2nd session, doc. 237, p. 42-50 (author's Drive); Tykal, Jack B., “Provost, Etienne”, Utah History Encyclopedia, Salt Lake City, University of Utah Press, 1994 (copy in the author's Drive, t_000690.pdf; uen.org)

properties.nom: With Audubon on the Omega, from St. Louis to Fort Union
properties.description: The American Fur Company steamboat Omega carries Audubon, his companions and his hunters, with Provost and his daughter, to Fort Union in seven weeks.
properties.sources: Audubon, Maria R. (ed.) (1897), Audubon and his Journals, New York, Scribner, vol. 2, p. 30-65; Vaugeois, Denis, “Provost, Québec - Provo, Salt Lake, Utah ? Des liens historiques et généalogiques”, Le Devoir, 16-17 February 2002 (clipping in the author's Drive, folder ETIENNE_PROVOST_AUDUBON)

properties.nom: Down the Missouri by mackinaw
properties.description: Audubon and his party go back down the Missouri in a mackinaw boat to St. Charles, where Provost goes ashore on October 18.
properties.sources: Vaugeois, Denis, “Provost, Québec - Provo, Salt Lake, Utah ? Des liens historiques et généalogiques”, Le Devoir, 16-17 February 2002 (clipping in the author's Drive, folder ETIENNE_PROVOST_AUDUBON); Audubon, Maria R. (ed.) (1897), Audubon and his Journals, New York, Scribner, vol. 2, p. 30-65

properties.nom: The last stretch, on foot
properties.description: Drunk and cheerful, Provost walks the twenty-odd miles from St. Charles to St. Louis.
properties.sources: Vaugeois, Denis, “Provost, Québec - Provo, Salt Lake, Utah ? Des liens historiques et généalogiques”, Le Devoir, 16-17 February 2002 (clipping in the author's Drive, folder ETIENNE_PROVOST_AUDUBON)

properties.nom: From Michilimackinac to St. Louis by Green Bay, the Fox, the Wisconsin and the Mississippi
properties.description: The « Southern Dependencies » of his contract opened the Mississippi road: Lake Michigan, Green Bay, the Fox River, the Wisconsin portage, Prairie du Chien, then down the Mississippi to St. Louis. Provost followed it between 1805, when he was hired, and 1814, when he was in St. Louis. This route replaces the one proposed by Bouchard and Lévesque (via Detroit and Chicago, about 1806-1810).
properties.sources: Société historique de Saint-Boniface, base de données des contrats des voyageurs (archivesshsb.mb.ca), fiche « Provost, Etienne », contrat du 25 janvier 1805 devant le notaire Jonathan A. Gray (BAnQ, microfilm M620/1535), consultée le 20 novembre 2026 ; Bouchard, Serge et Marie-Christine Lévesque (2014), Ils ont couru l'Amérique. De remarquables oubliés, t. 2, Montréal, Lux, chap. « Hommes des montagnes : Provost, Chalifoux, Robidoux » (epub du Drive de l'auteur) ; Havard, Gilles (2019), L'Amérique fantôme. Les aventuriers francophones du Nouveau Monde, Paris, Flammarion, ch. 8 « L'homme des montagnes : Étienne Provost », p. 323-379 (PDF du Drive de l'auteur, dossier GILLES_HAVARD, lu intégralement le 19 nov. 2026)
properties.note: Schematic route; date of arrival in St. Louis unknown.
